title: Voice for Animals (Independent Office of Animal Welfare) Bill 2013 [No. 2]

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish an Office of Animal Welfare as a Commonwealth statutory authority to advise on animal welfare in activities regulated by the Commonwealth.
Its chief executive would review livestock export standards, supply chain assurance and departmental enforcement, supported by an advisory committee and staff undertaking inquiries and research.
Reports and recommendations would go to the Minister for tabling in Parliament with written responses, including possible advice on aligning Commonwealth, state and territory laws.
changes: The Minister could direct the chief executive on performing their functions, and compliance would be mandatory.
An advisory committee would include welfare organisations, consumers, scientists, ethicists, departmental representatives and commercial animal interests.
The office would have to produce an annual report for parliamentary tabling.
The chief executive could delegate functions and powers to staff.
summary.affected: Animal welfare organisations, consumer groups, relevant scientists and ethicists, departmental officials and commercial producers or purchasers of animals or animal products are affected.
